page: Microsoft Azure E96nds_v6 is an x86_64 virtualization instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V, categorized under the memory-optimized Endv6 family. It supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel processor, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include GPU accelerators.

For local I/O demands, the instance bundles 5,670 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage. The architecture is explicitly network optimized and features zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking mechanisms for public routing.

Hardware resource allocation delivers significant density for large-scale enterprise deployments. Cost efficiency is defined by the consolidation of substantial memory capacity alongside 5.6 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage on a single system, mitigating the need for multiple smaller nodes or separate external storage volumes for caching and temporary scratch disks.

The primary tradeoff of the E96nds_v6 resides in its dedicated, heavy-footprint architecture, making it less appropriate for horizontally scalable stateless workloads. Instead, the balance of 96 cores, 768.0 GB RAM, and dense NVMe disk space targets large in-memory databases, real-time analytics platforms, enterprise relational database systems, and heavy ETL processing pipelines.
